kept.excerpt: Neither Bradley Barcola nor Ibrahim Mbaye travelled for PSG’s French Super Cup match against Lens, with Liverpool in talks to sign both. Liverpool were reported to be planning a new bid for Barcola, although PSG’s £145 million asking price remained an obstacle. Asked for an update, Luis Enrique said: “I will speak about the transfer window when it is finished.”
kept.relevance: Provides cutoff-day reporting on negotiations, Barcola’s squad omission and the unresolved transfer fee.

kept.excerpt: Barcola and Mbaye were omitted from PSG’s 20-man matchday squad against Lens. RMC Sport journalist Fabrice Hawkins reported that both players were on their way out and that discussions over moves to Liverpool would continue the following week.
kept.relevance: Documents a recent squad omission and attributes the reported continuation of transfer discussions to a named RMC Sport journalist.

kept.excerpt: Liverpool’s pursuit of Barcola remained ongoing, with PSG seeking a deal worth £145 million and Liverpool willing to pay around £102.6 million. Barcola was an unused substitute in PSG’s UEFA Super Cup win over Aston Villa. Luis Enrique said that when a player is unhappy at the club, a solution needs to be found.
kept.relevance: Identifies the reported valuation gap immediately before the cutoff and supplies contemporaneous comments from PSG’s coach.

kept.excerpt: According to Belgian journalist Sacha Tavolieri, Barcola had agreed personal terms with Liverpool for a five-year contract. Liverpool had not agreed a transfer fee with Paris Saint-Germain. PSG’s pursuit of Ajax winger Mika Godts was described as a possible factor in enabling Barcola’s departure.
kept.relevance: Separates a reported agreement with the player from the still-unresolved agreement between clubs.

kept.excerpt: Luis Enrique included Liverpool targets Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye in PSG’s squad for the UEFA Super Cup against Aston Villa. The match was scheduled for Wednesday, August 12.
kept.relevance: Establishes that Barcola remained involved in PSG’s squad shortly before his subsequent omission against Lens.

kept.excerpt: PSG’s signing of Maghnes Akliouche from Monaco could coincide with Barcola’s departure. Barcola, who scored three goals at the World Cup, was heavily linked with Liverpool.
kept.relevance: Supplies independent wire-service reporting on Liverpool interest and PSG’s recruitment of another attacking player.

kept.excerpt: Liverpool had held preliminary talks with PSG and Barcola’s representatives, but a significant valuation gap remained, with PSG valuing him at £145 million. Barcola had two years left on his contract and had indicated he would not sign a new one; a move to Liverpool was said to appeal to him. PSG would ideally keep Barcola, and their incoming wingers were not considered his replacements.
kept.relevance: Provides detailed reporting on the principal financial obstacle, the player’s reported preference and PSG’s preference to retain him.

kept.excerpt: Arsenal had shown interest in Barcola, who had two years remaining on his PSG contract and showed no signs of wanting to renew. PSG’s £145 million valuation could present a problem for Arsenal.
kept.relevance: Documents a potential alternative acquiring club and the financial constraint affecting that possibility.

search_notes: Frozen cutoff: 2026-08-17. Included only items with explicit publication dates on or before that date; excluded later-dated reporting, undated pages, betting pages and prediction-market material. Excerpts are factual paraphrases of source text available in web-search results, preserving attribution for transfer claims. Direct web_fetch failed because of a provider configuration error; the requested agent-reach web-read fallback returned RATE_LIMITED, so full-page retrieval could not be completed. Targeted web searches supplied publication dates and article passages. Liverpool FC's dated Media Watch reproduction of The Standard was treated as a duplicate media report, not as an official transfer announcement. No forecast or resolution determination is supplied.
